card werk-cli-name  [decided]
Agents call the CLI by the plain name werk, in every project
why: werk gives its instructions and subagents to agents in every project, so the text must name the CLI the same way everywhere. A path into werk's own source exists only in werk's repository.

Every instruction, subagent and permission rule writes the CLI as `werk`. werk keeps a launcher named `werk` in a folder of its own and puts that folder first on the PATH of every agent it starts. In dev mode the launcher runs the CLI of the checkout whose code is running, so each call uses the current code. In production it runs the installed program. The person's own terminal does not get it.

A `werk` command writes to the map of the nearest folder at or above the current folder that has a map. With no such folder it fails with an error. An agent starts in its project's root folder, so its commands reach its own project's map.

  -> refines         werk-cli  The CLI is the agent's interface to the map. Each command's form lives on one card under it
  -> depends_on      werk-agent-instructions  Every agent that can write to the map reads the werk agent instructions, in any project
       why: the instructions that name the CLI go to agents in every project
  -> depends_on      werk-projects-one-process  One server process holds every project, so one code reload reaches all of them
       why: each agent belongs to one project of the one server, and its commands must reach that project's map
  <- alternative_to  werk-cli-name:opt0  Write the absolute path of the running CLI into the prompt
Options
  werk-cli-name:opt0  Write the absolute path of the running CLI into the prompt
    why not: The text then differs per machine and per mode, and every prompt and subagent file needs a placeholder. One plain name reads the same everywhere.

The prototype now matches #werk-cli-name. One spot did not match: the builder prompt.

- **Mismatch:** `src/build-prompt.ts` wrote the CLI into every builder prompt as `"<bun path>" "<src/cli.ts path>"`. That is the absolute-path option the card rejects (`werk-cli-name:opt0`).
- **Fix:** the prompt now writes `werk`. Builder agents already get the `bin/werk` launcher first on their PATH, and `Bash` is open for them. I removed the unused path code.
- **Tests:** `build-prompt.test.ts` now checks that the prompt has `werk search` and no absolute path. `build.test.ts` now runs `werk add` and `werk followed` through the PATH launcher. I ran both files: 74 pass, 0 fail. `tsc` is clean, and lint shows no new warning.

The rest already matched the card:
- The `bin/werk` launcher exists and runs the checkout's own CLI.
- `agentEnv` puts it first on the PATH of every agent werk starts.
- The chat agent allows `Bash(werk:*)`.
- `prompts/agent.md` uses `werk`.

I left three uses of the full path alone. They are not agent text:
- `plan.ts` spawns the CLI itself, internally.
- `AGENTS.md` has commands for a person's terminal, and the card says that terminal does not get the launcher.
- `.claude/settings.local.json` is your personal permission file.

Next: run `bun run test` to check the whole suite. I only ran the two build test files.
